We have a quick compliance question as we're evaluating Redwood for a patient intake feature. Our mobile app streams short audio clips (live intake) to your API for real-time transcription. Our legal team asked for SOC2 evidence and a draft BAA to start the review. Happy to share a sanitized example of the payload if that helps.

Hi Susan — thanks, quick answers and options below. Attaching our SOC 2 Type II report (redacted) and a BAA template for your legal team to review.

Summary (short):
- Hosted (public API): by default is NOT eligible for PHI/BAA in our standard offering. Tokens and request/response metadata may traverse shared control-plane services and we require Dedicated or Private deployments for HIPAA workloads.
- Dedicated: provides isolated GPU pools and the option to disable request retention, lock logs to per-customer storage, and integrate with your KMS for envelope encryption. We can sign a BAA for Dedicated and Private customers.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): recommended for full PHI scope and supports HSM/KMS, audit log export, and strict egress controls.

Notes on streaming transcriptions:
- Real-time audio is processed by the inference runtime; by default runtime holds ephemeral state (KV cache) in memory and does not persist audio or token streams unless retention/observability is enabled.
- If you use presigned S3 uploads for raw audio and configure Redwood to pull from your bucket, you retain primary custody of raw data; we still process the audio and generate transcripts, which we consider customer data and therefore PHI if the audio contains identifiers.
- For PHI use cases, our recommended patterns: Dedicated deployment with retention disabled or private deployment with customer-managed keys.

Attachments included: SOC2-TypeII-report-2026.pdf, Redwood-BAA-template-CarePort.docx

Next steps:
1) If you can share a sanitized dataflow (or the sample payload you referenced) we can map the processing boundary.
2) I can schedule a technical call with our Solutions Architect to walk streaming options and produce a recommended config.
3) Legal can take the attached BAA and start redlines.

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Question — streaming transcription & BAA

Hi Susan — quick security clarification from our side. Short answer: hosted public API is not available for PHI under our standard terms. Presigned S3 uploads do not automatically make hosted eligible — the key factor is whether the customer and Redwood can enforce isolation and retention controls required by HIPAA. If raw audio is staged in your S3 bucket and Redwood pulls it into a shared hosted runtime, that still crosses our shared-control boundary and we will advise Dedicated or Private for PHI.

Technical specifics:
- Streaming runtime: audio frames are ingested into the inference runtime and in-memory KV cache is used for context; we do not persist raw audio or token streams unless observability/retention flags are enabled on the tenant.
- Retention controls: Dedicated/private customers can opt out of request/response logging and configure zero retention; hosted customers cannot fully opt out today.
- Key management: Private and Dedicated support customer-managed KMS keys (AWS KMS/HSM) and exportable audit logs for compliance review.
- Evidence & delivery: SOC2 Type II (attached) and architectural diagram (attached: streaming-dataflow.png). Our legal team is rdl-legal@redwood.ai — please copy them on BAA redlines.

Recommended next step: schedule a 30–45min call with Solutions (Monica) + Security (me) so we can map the dataflow and propose a Dedicated deployment quote and BAA. Once we have the sanitized payload you mentioned, we can produce a processing-boundary diagram showing exactly where PHI crosses customer vs Redwood services.
